newsitem.title: HONG KONG: North Korean trade office to open in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: North Korean trade office to open in Hong Kong.

text.p: North Korea said on Tuesday it would open a representative office in Hong Kong in the wake of an unprecedented visit by a team promoting its special trade zones.

A statement issued by the office, operated by the Committee for Promotion of External Economic Cooperation, will deal with trade enquiries and issue invitations to those wishing to visit the Rajin Sonbong Free Trade and economic zone.
The representative office is on premises occupied by Young's Trading and Investment (H.K.) Ltd, which acts as a conduit for North-South Korean trade in the absence of direct links.
The two Koreas remain technically at war more than four decades after the Korean War ended in an armistice.
North Korea sent a trade delegation to Hong Kong and Japan last month to seeking foreign funding in its free zones.

Delegation leader Kim Jong-u told Hong Kong investors the country's ruling Workers Party had switched the focus away from heavy industry to attracting investment in light industry, particularly electronics and automation, foreign trade and agriculture.
